Marcos: Heads-up: we're enforcing the Streaming Chunk Schema v1.1 across all SDKs and the hosted API. This is a compatibility-sensitive change; please read the rollout summary below.

Priya: Short summary for docs teams: schema v1.1 stabilizes the chunk envelope for streaming (adds 'chunk_id', standardizes 'event' field values, and requires 'final' boolean when a stream closes). We'll publish a migration guide + JSON examples.

Jules: Support note: this will affect customer integrations that parse raw chunks. We'll prepare a canned response, a quick detector script, and sample fallback logic.

Marcos: What changes:
- Each stream chunk will be a single JSON object per line (newline-delimited JSON).
- Required fields: "chunk_id" (uuid), "event" (one of: "delta", "meta", "done"), "payload" (object).
- Final chunk must include "event": "done" and "final": true.

Katrina: Platform impact: load balancers and edge caching are unaffected. We did add a defensive parser in the runtime to drop malformed chunks and emit a short metric (stream.parse.error). That will be opt-in for Dedicated in case teams rely on old loose parsing.

Marcos: Example parsing pseudocode (JS):
```js
// safe ndjson parser
const rl = require('readline').createInterface({ input: res.body });
for await (const line of rl) {
  if (!line.trim()) continue;
  try {
    const obj = JSON.parse(line);
    handleChunk(obj);
  } catch (e) {
    metrics.increment('stream.parse.error');
  }
}
```

Priya: Docs will include: 1) quick migration checklist, 2) before/after sample payloads, 3) compatibility FAQ, 4) integration snippets for py/js/go, 5) a short note for partners on proxies/NGINX config. Draft goes to #docs-review tomorrow.

Marcos: SDK changes: py/js/go will add helpers: StreamChunk.from_line(line) and a ChunkValidator. Breaking behavior: older SDKs that relied on chunk ordering-only may still work, but code that expects mixed types in "payload" now must look at "event" first. We will bump minor semver (e.g., 3.2.x -> 3.3.0) to indicate the stricter parsing.

Jules: Migration playbook for Support:
- Detect clients: look for patterns in logs ("parse error" metric or raw newline commas).
- Offer a quick patch snippet to replace naive JSON scans with the provided parser helper.
- If customer can't upgrade, we can enable a temporary "compat-mode" on Dedicated for up to 30 days.

Katrina: Rollout timeline:
- Day 0 (today): Announce + docs draft.
- Day 3: SDK preview releases (alpha) and compatibility checker CLI.
- Day 10: GA SDK releases + docs published.
- Day 10-40: 30-day migration window; default hosted endpoints will begin enforcing strict schema parsing at Day 40.
- Day 40+: Strict enforcement; compat-mode only via support request for Dedicated customers.

Marcos: API note for integrators: if you are using proxies that buffer streams (e.g., some HTTP proxies), add these headers to avoid buffering: "Cache-Control: no-transform" and "Connection: keep-alive". We'll add this to the docs.

Priya: I'll add a short "What to do if you see truncated streams" section: suggest switching to the helper parser, checking proxy buffering, and validating chunk sizes (we cap payload at 256KB).

Marcos: PR links: JS preview: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/3150 (alpha), Py preview: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/4021 (alpha). Please don't merge until QA signoff.

Jules: Internal playbook: patch KB article ID 7891, add detection dashboard in Observability (stream.parse.error alert), and queue a support rotation to monitor incoming tickets during Day 10-40.

Katrina: Ops: we will run a canary for 48h on 5% of traffic with strict parsing turned on on hosted, then roll to 100% if no regressions. We'll post canary metrics to #release-health.

Marcos: Thanks — please react with :eyes: when you've read and leave questions. I'll follow up with a short video walkthrough for SDK authors tomorrow.
